designedAgainst.note: Design only. No runtime module imports this file; nothing here is available to a learner. Product availability requires all seven master-contract gates, not this file alone.

canDo: read a dense, abstract or argumentative text and reconstruct its claim, its support, and what it leaves unstated
reformulate that material precisely for a different, named audience without flattening its nuance or inventing certainty the source lacks
notice when a message means more, less, or something other than its literal words, and respond in a way that shows they noticed
deliberately shift register to fit a stated audience and purpose, and edit their own text when its tone is wrong for that purpose
build an extended, qualified argument, anticipate the strongest counter-argument, and concede what deserves conceding without abandoning the position
keep a long, topic-shifting exchange coherent and repair a misunderstanding at the level of what someone meant, not only what they typed
stay functional inside an unfamiliar or high-ambiguity exchange rather than defaulting to a rehearsed script
mediate between two people, or two texts, who disagree, carrying each side's position faithfully and closing the exchange usefully
cannotYet: listening, speaking, live spoken interaction or pronunciation of any kind — out of product scope, not a level ceiling
real-time simultaneous or consecutive interpretation between languages
specialist professional registers this product has no domain expertise to validate: legal drafting, medical documentation, diplomatic protocol
creative/literary composition as an art form
native-speaker sociocultural intuition acquired only through lived immersion
any claim equivalent to an external CEFR examination certificate
definition.interactionCeiling: long, topic-shifting, occasionally unfamiliar or high-ambiguity exchanges, evaluated at paragraph/multi-turn scale, with repair available at the level of intention rather than only wording, and support fading strictly by evidence rather than by level label

Building and defending a nuanced position

canDos.why: Everything else in the level assumes the learner can pull a claim and its support out of a text that does not hand them over plainly. Without this, reformulation, synthesis and rebuttal all have nothing reliable to work from.
cefrRefs: Reading for Information and Argument C2

canDos.why: A single text's claim is only half the level's actual demand: C2 readers reconcile sources that disagree, which is also what the capstone mediation task needs on the input side.
cefrRefs: Reading for Information and Argument C2

canDos.why: A claim without its writer's degree of commitment is half-read. This is the level's first explicit encounter with evidentiality, which register and mediation both depend on later.
cefrRefs: Reading for Information and Argument C2

canDos.why: The product's first task combining dense-text extraction with audience reformulation: carrying meaning across an audience gap without losing or inventing certainty, from a source the learner had to synthesize rather than one already handed to them in conversation. This escalates C1's reformulate_for_a_different_audience (a spoken/conversational reformulation) with source-text density and audience ambiguity C1 does not require; it is reuse and escalation, not a second introduction of the same capability (LC-AUD-001 F3). Everything downstream that needs 'say this again, but for someone else' depends on it.
Compression is where nuance is usually lost first. This is the capability that proves a summary can be short and still honest about hedges and disagreement.

The small-scale sibling of reformulation: restating a single sentence without collapsing its precision. Should rather than required because the level's mediation core is already carried by the two required capabilities above.
The level's central pragmatic skill: language that means more than it says. Register control, face-saving disagreement and mediation all assume the learner can already notice this.
The hardest, most explicitly C2 case of implied meaning, and the one every CEFR C2 descriptor names by name ('distinguish fine shades of meaning ... irony').
Noticing an implication (recognize_implied_meaning) is receptive; this is the productive half — responding to an indirect request or refusal the way it was actually meant, not its literal wording.
The level's other central pragmatic skill: choosing form on purpose to fit an audience and purpose, rather than defaulting to one register regardless of who is listening.

Register is not only word choice; it is also how much certainty a speaker signals. This is the level's explicit hedging/boosting control, proportionate to actual certainty rather than habitual overuse of either pole.
Disagreement is where register control matters most in real use. This integrates the arc's register work with the previous arc's implication work into one recognizably social skill.
C1 already argues with reasons; C2 sustains that argument across more ground and qualifies it so it does not overclaim, which is the difference between an opinion and a defensible position.

A position that never meets its strongest objection is not yet a C2-level argument. This is also the capability the mediation capstone leans on hardest, since mediating means representing the other side's strongest point too.
The fine-grained sibling of soften_or_intensify_a_claim, applied across a whole argument rather than one sentence: knowing exactly how far a position can be pushed without overclaiming.

The first level where 'the conversation changed subject and the learner kept it coherent' is itself the graded evidence, not incidental. It is what separates C2 fluency from a string of well-formed but disconnected turns.
canDos.unresolvedPrerequisiteNote: c1_assumed__handle_abstract_topics is LC-AUD-001's F6 low-confidence row: the audit's candidate match is c1.sustain_a_conversation_across_topic_shifts, but that C1 capability itself still rests on an unresolved-at-audit-time B2 placeholder chain, so a mechanical rename was deliberately NOT applied here. This needs an explicit human curriculum-design decision, not an automated fix (LC-AUD-001 openQuestionsForHumanReview). Left as the original placeholder id until that decision is made.

canDos.why: Every earlier level repairs at the word or form level. C2 repairs at the level of what someone meant — the harder, genuinely new skill, and a direct prerequisite for the mediation capstone.
C2 evidence must include sustained, varied, unfamiliar, high-ambiguity tasks, not just narrow prompt-response success. This capability names that requirement directly rather than leaving it implicit.

Every earlier arc produces language; this is the first arc where revising it on purpose — not producing a better first draft, but noticing and fixing a wrong tone or an imprecise word — is itself the tested skill.

Repeating the same word/structure across a long response is a C2-relevant flatness problem even when each sentence is individually correct. A closed, locally-checkable repetition detector makes this affordable to test.

A natural extension of register shifting to a whole text's genre (e.g., turning a casual note into a formal notice), kept optional because the required register work is already fully evidenced by shift_register_deliberately and edit_own_text_for_precision_and_tone.

The level's capstone and graduation-critical integrative proof: represent two disagreeing sides faithfully to a third party, without editorializing, using synthesis, register control, argument-tracking and intention-level repair together in one extended, high-ambiguity task — LinguaChat's arrange_to_meet-equivalent for C2.

explicitExclusions.why: Voice/media are out of product scope entirely (CLAUDE.md infrastructure boundaries), not a level-specific ceiling.
A distinct professional skill this product does not teach or evaluate.
Legal drafting, medical documentation, diplomatic protocol and discipline-specific academic writing conventions require domain expertise this product cannot validate honestly.
C2 here is high-precision communicative control, not creative-writing craft.
Regional slang currency, generational idiom and lived-context humor are acquired through immersion, not a learnable pragmatic pattern this product can teach.
LinguaChat's own runtime evidence is not, and must never be marketed as, an external CEFR examination certificate.

patterns.form: it could be argued that / arguably / to some extent / not necessarily
patterns.renameNote: Renamed by LC-AUD-001 F11 / LC-FND-002: this id previously reused B2's hedging_pattern for a structurally different, more formal/academic form (B2's hedging_pattern: 'sort of / tend to / I'd say / more or less'). The two are different registers of hedging, not the same grammatical structure recurring, so crediting one against a spaced-retrieval record seeded by the other would credit language the learner was never taught. B2's hedging_pattern id is unchanged.

patterns.form: undeniably / there is little doubt that / it is clear that
while X has merit, ... / granted that..., nevertheless... / even so
presumably / ostensibly / allegedly / according to X
in other words / to put it another way / put simply, for a non-specialist
matched formal/neutral/informal lexical and syntactic pairs for the same proposition
I take your point, but... / that's fair, though I'd push back on...
insofar as / whereby / that said / by the same token
recognizing litotes, rhetorical questions and deliberate understatement as carrying an inverted or reduced literal meaning
replacing a vague/repeated item with a precise, non-repeating collocate

proposed.whyNotExisting: A source text carries a claim and support that must be extracted, not a single named value; no existing slot type holds multi-sentence content with an internal argument structure.
A person is an interlocutor identity; an audience profile is a target-audience descriptor for a text and must not be substitutable for a conversational partner.
Must be a closed enum so the evaluator can check a requested shift actually occurred, unlike free-text slots elsewhere in the product.
Tracked as its own type so the evaluator can check presence/appropriateness of a hedge or boost independently of the proposition it attaches to.

explicitlyNotNeeded.why: C2 evaluation needs to know what is implied and how certain the speaker is, not a coarse positive/negative sentiment number.
Ambiguity/novelty is already carried by evidence type (transfer, delayed retrieval, unfamiliar exchange), not a separate numeric slot.

intentStrategy.rule: One intent per communicative function; variants travel as a subtype on the step payload, exactly as lower levels already carry repairKind/quantityForm/thingId — not as a new intent. No arc introduces more than three new intents.
intentStrategy.explosionGuard: If an arc's design needs more than three new intents, the arc is teaching phrases rather than a capability. Every arc above stays at or under three.

evaluationStrategy.rule: The canonical frame is always judged locally first; escalation is for a reply that is inconclusive, exactly as lower levels already route it. No capability is designed to depend on a live provider being reachable. Every hybrid intent must have a deterministic local/fake-provider fixture path so CI proves routing correctness with zero real model calls, per ai/provider_policy.py — see coreEngineRequirements #2.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner meets an argumentative or abstract text and cannot reliably say what it actually claims, what it uses to support that claim, or what it deliberately leaves unstated.
arcs.whyNow: Every later arc — reformulation, argument, mediation — assumes the learner can already do this on the input side.
arcs.autonomyTarget: model excerpt and a scaffolded claim/support frame available on first exposure; withheld once independent evidence exists
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided claim-and-support extractions plus one on a genuinely unseen source text
arcs.transferTarget: an unseen source text in an unrelated topic area
arcs.risk: Dense text can slide into a reading-comprehension quiz that tests topic knowledge instead of the capability. Every task must be answerable from the text alone, regardless of the learner's prior knowledge of the subject.

arcs.titleConcept: Saying it precisely, for someone else
arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can extract a claim but cannot yet hand it to somebody else without either dumbing it down past honesty or leaving it too dense for that audience.
arcs.whyNow: Mediation is the level's organizing idea; this arc is its first productive test, directly after the receptive arc that feeds it.
arcs.neutralFallback: a workplace memo reformulated for a new colleague
arcs.autonomyTarget: audience profile and a partial frame available early; withheld once independent + transfer evidence exists
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided reformulations that preserve the source's hedge/certainty level, plus one transfer instance
arcs.transferTarget: a new source text/audience pairing not used in teaching
arcs.risk: The evaluator must be able to tell 'shorter and still honest' from 'shorter and overconfident' — dropping a hedge is the single most likely near-miss failure mode and must be explicitly tested.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can restate literal content but misses meaning carried by implication, understatement or irony — and cannot yet respond in a way that shows they caught it.
arcs.whyNow: Register control and face-saving disagreement, the next two arcs, both assume the learner can already notice implied meaning.
arcs.neutralFallback: a neutral workplace or service exchange carrying an indirect refusal
arcs.autonomyTarget: explicit 'what might this really mean' cue available early; withheld once independent evidence exists, restored quickly after a miss given how high-strain this task is
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided implication identifications plus one unaided appropriate response to an indirect speech act
arcs.transferTarget: an unseen exchange carrying an unfamiliar implicature
arcs.delayedRetrievalTarget: retrieved unaided inside arc 6 and arc 8
arcs.risk: Irony and understatement are the level's highest false-positive risk: a learner can guess an ironic reading without real evidence. Distractor items (a literal reading that is also plausible) are required, not optional.

arcs.titleConcept: Saying it the right way for the moment
arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can be correct and still land wrong for a formal, informal, or professional situation, and cannot yet dial certainty up or down on purpose.
arcs.whyNow: Argument and discourse-flexibility, the next two arcs, both need register and hedge/boost control already in place.
arcs.neutralFallback: same neutral workplace/service situations used for every learner
arcs.autonomyTarget: a target register/hedge level stated explicitly at first; the learner infers the appropriate level unaided once evidence supports it
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided register shifts to a stated target, two unaided proportionate hedge/boost uses
arcs.transferTarget: a new audience/register pairing not used in teaching
arcs.delayedRetrievalTarget: retrieved unaided inside arc 6 and arc 8
arcs.risk: This is the level's densest new-device arc (four infrastructure groups). The task explicitly requires neutral, non-personalized contexts (§7 of the blueprint) precisely because register control must be provable independent of topic familiarity.

arcs.titleConcept: Building and defending a nuanced position
arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can state an opinion but not yet sustain it across pushback, qualify how far it goes, or concede a real point without abandoning the position.
arcs.whyNow: It needs the hedge/boost control just taught, and it is what the discourse-flexibility arc's coherence-under-topic-shift task will be tested through.
arcs.autonomyTarget: a counterargument is surfaced explicitly at first; the learner must anticipate it unaided once independent evidence exists
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided extended arguments including a genuine concession, plus one unaided rebuttal of an unseen counterargument
arcs.transferTarget: an unseen debate topic and an unseen counterargument
arcs.risk: Rebuttal-without-any-concession is the near-miss failure mode most likely to slip through a naive evaluator; the evaluation requirements (§11) explicitly flag it as pragmatically inappropriate, not just stylistically weaker.

arcs.titleConcept: Keeping a long, unpredictable exchange coherent
arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can handle one topic well but loses coherence when a conversation shifts subject, and can repair a misheard word but not a misunderstood intention.
arcs.whyNow: It is the level's fluency/discourse-management arc, deliberately placed after the learner already owns argument, register and implication separately, so it can put them under real conversational pressure.
arcs.neutralFallback: a neutral multi-topic exchange (a shared-flat dispute that drifts from a chore schedule into money)
arcs.autonomyTarget: support fades fastest here once independent evidence exists, since replayed rehearsal defeats the point of an unfamiliar-exchange test
arcs.evidenceTarget: one unaided coherent exchange across at least two topic shifts, one unaided intention-level repair, one unaided pass through a genuinely unfamiliar exchange
arcs.transferTarget: an unfamiliar-exchange scenario not used in teaching, by construction
arcs.risk: The single hardest arc to evaluate deterministically. This is the primary driver behind coreEngineRequirements #1 (multi-turn evaluation span) — without it this arc cannot be graded honestly.

arcs.titleConcept: Shaping your own language on purpose
arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner produces correct language but does not yet review and adjust their own text the way a careful C2 writer does — for precision, for tone, and for not repeating themselves into flatness.
arcs.whyNow: It is deliberately placed after register and argument work exist to edit, and right before the capstone, which assumes the learner can self-correct rather than submit a first draft.
arcs.neutralFallback: editing a neutral notice/message rather than a hobby text
arcs.autonomyTarget: a flagged sentence/word available early ('this might sound too casual here'); withheld once independent evidence exists
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided edits that measurably improve precision or tone-fit, one unaided repetition fix
arcs.transferTarget: an unseen draft with an unfamiliar tone mismatch
arcs.risk: Editing tasks can degrade into a proofreading exercise that only catches grammar errors. The task must specifically require noticing tone/precision problems in an otherwise grammatically correct draft.

arcs.titleConcept: Standing between two people who disagree
arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner has each separate skill — synthesis, reformulation, register, argument-tracking, intention-level repair — but has not yet had to combine all of them, unaided, inside one extended, high-ambiguity, unfamiliar task, which is exactly what real C2 mediation demands.
arcs.whyNow: It is the level's capstone by design, placed last so it can require transfer and delayed retrieval of nearly everything the level taught.
arcs.neutralFallback: a neutral landlord/tenant or community-notice disagreement, deliberately unfamiliar in its exact particulars
arcs.autonomyTarget: no support surfaced by default; this is the level's proof point for independent + transfer + delayed-retrieval evidence across nearly every required capability
arcs.evidenceTarget: one unaided full mediation task representing both sides faithfully and proposing a next step, plus at least one delayed-retrieval instance of each of the four prerequisite capabilities inside the same task
arcs.transferTarget: a disagreement scenario and source materials never used in any earlier arc, by construction
arcs.delayedRetrievalTarget: the arc's entire purpose: every required capability from arcs 1–7 retrieved unaided here
arcs.risk: The single point where coreEngineRequirements #4 (multiple delayed-retrieval records inside one task) becomes load-bearing; without that shared-engine capability this arc cannot record its own graduation evidence honestly.

coreEngineRequirements.problem: Several C2 intents (sustain_coherence, repair_at_intention_level, mediate_disagreement) need evaluation across a span of turns, not just the latest learner message.
coreEngineRequirements.whyCurrentEngineCannot: Evaluation as understood from the A1/Pre-A1 runtime is per-turn.
coreEngineRequirements.earliestLevelNeeded: c2 (to be confirmed against b2/c1 blueprints, which may need it earlier)
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: An optional span-evaluation mode invoked when an intent declares evaluationSpan: "multiTurn".
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: Must not change per-turn evaluation for any existing level.
testsRequired: regression suite proving lower levels unaffected when the mode is unused

coreEngineRequirements.problem: recognize_implication, shift_register and qualify_claim are hard to judge with pure string matching, but CI/QA must stay provider-free.
coreEngineRequirements.whyCurrentEngineCannot: Hybrid evaluation already escalates inconclusive replies to a remote judge for lower levels, but C2 leans on this far more heavily and needs deterministic CI coverage without any real model call.
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: Extend the local/fake provider fixture set with deterministic canned judgments for every new C2 hybrid intent, mirroring the existing hybrid path for lower-level intents such as introduce_person.
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: None to lower levels if implemented as additive fixtures.
testsRequired: fixture-driven tests proving every new C2 intent has a working local/fake evaluation path with zero real provider calls, matching ai/provider_policy.py's existing guarantee

coreEngineRequirements.problem: No existing semantic type represents a multi-sentence reading passage or a named target audience for reformulation.
coreEngineRequirements.whyCurrentEngineCannot: Existing scene-content payloads assume short, single-value slots.
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: Add the source_text and audience_profile semantic types (see semanticTypes.proposed) plus scene-content support for a longer passage than current levels assume.
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: Scene rendering/i18n must not silently break for shorter existing scenes.
testsRequired: i18n coverage for the new content shape

coreEngineRequirements.problem: The capstone intentionally requires delayed retrieval of several earlier required capabilities inside a single extended task.
coreEngineRequirements.whyCurrentEngineCannot: No existing episode records more than one distinct delayedRetrieval evidence entry per completion.
coreEngineRequirements.proposedSharedBehaviour: Allow one episode/task completion to log multiple distinct delayedRetrieval evidence records against different canDoIds.
coreEngineRequirements.regressionRisk: Learner-model schema change must be additive only; existing single-capability episodes must record identically.
testsRequired: learner-model schema tests proving old single-capability episodes are unaffected
coreEngineRequirements.note: RESOLVED by LC-INT-001: learnerModel.js's recordDelayedRetrievalEvidence(model, canDoIds, ...) accepts an array and logs a distinct delayedRetrievalAt timestamp per capability id from one completion, additive to the existing single-capability path; wired live from EpisodeShell.jsx, not dead code. See docs/curriculum/final-supervisor-acceptance.md section 3.

no unprepared jump: every C2 new discourse device genuinely builds on a C1-proven capability
no duplicated 'new' capability already taught at C1 (this blueprint's patterns table must be corrected if C1 already teaches basic hedging or register awareness)

complexity rises coherently from C1 into C2
graduation evidence declared in this blueprint is attainable through real runtime paths once LC-CONT-C2 exists

humanPilotQuestions: Does a C2-level learner experience the hedging/boosting and register-pair distinctions as meaningfully different, or do they collapse them into 'more formal words' without real pragmatic control?
Does the mediation capstone feel like a realistic high-stakes task in a chat-mediated, asynchronous-feeling product, compared to how C2 learners actually need this skill at work or in writing?
Is text-only irony/understatement recognition transferable to spoken irony if this product ever implements listening, or is it a narrower skill that should be labeled as such?
Does explicit teaching of stance markers produce natural-sounding use, or does it produce learners who over-hedge/over-mark stance in a way that itself reads as unnatural?
Do learners perceive the capstone's delayed-retrieval-of-many-capabilities design as a fair integrative test, or as an unfair difficulty pile-up at the very end of the level?
Is a 390px chat surface actually comfortable for dense source_text reading tasks at C2, or does the product need a distinct reading-mode presentation?
